_about: Short cheat sheet for the commands in the Linux & OS section. Examples are for GNU/Linux.

commands.name: grep
commands.what: Search text for lines that match a pattern.
examples: grep -rn "ERROR" /var/log/myapp/   # search recursively, show line numbers
grep -i "timeout" app.log          # ignore upper/lower case
grep -v "DEBUG" app.log            # lines that do NOT match
grep -c "404" access.log           # count matching lines

commands.name: awk
commands.what: Work with columns (fields) in text, line by line.
examples: awk '{print $1}' access.log          # first column of each line
awk -F, '$3 > 100 {print $1}' d.csv # comma-separated; filter by column 3
awk 'NR==10' file.txt               # print line 10

commands.name: sed
commands.what: Stream editor: find and replace or pick lines from text.
examples: sed 's/http:/https:/g' links.txt    # replace every match on each line
sed -n '10p' file.txt               # print only line 10
sed -i 's/old/new/g' config.txt     # edit the file in place (GNU sed)

commands.name: find
commands.what: Find files by name, type, size, or age.
examples: find . -name "*.log"                # files ending in .log
find /tmp -type f -size +100M       # files bigger than 100 MB
find . -name "*.tmp" -mtime +7      # .tmp files changed more than 7 days ago

commands.name: ps
commands.what: Show a snapshot of running processes.
examples: ps aux                              # every process, with CPU and memory use
ps aux | grep nginx                 # find a specific process
ps -ef --forest                     # show parent/child tree

commands.name: top
commands.what: Live view of processes and system load.
examples: top                                 # press q to quit
# inside top: P sorts by CPU, M sorts by memory, k kills a process

commands.name: kill
commands.what: Send a signal to a process (by default SIGTERM, a polite stop request).
examples: kill 1234                           # SIGTERM: ask process 1234 to stop
kill -9 1234                        # SIGKILL: force stop, no cleanup
pkill -f myscript.py                # signal processes by name/command

commands.name: systemctl
examples: systemctl status nginx              # is it running? recent log lines
sudo systemctl restart nginx        # restart a service
sudo systemctl enable nginx         # start automatically at boot

commands.name: journalctl
examples: journalctl -u nginx                 # logs for one service
journalctl -u nginx --since "1 hour ago"
journalctl -f                       # follow new log lines live

commands.name: cron
commands.what: Run commands on a schedule. Edit your schedule with crontab -e.
examples: # minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week  command
0 2 * * * /home/me/backup.sh        # every day at 02:00
*/15 * * * * /home/me/check.sh      # every 15 minutes
crontab -l                          # list your scheduled jobs
